cleanIntro: A break-action CVA cleans in three pieces — forend, barrel, breech plug — and the breech plug is the whole job. ⛔ Muzzleloading fouling is corrosive, so this is not a chore that waits for the weekend. A Nitride-treated barrel buys you about a week; a plain stainless one buys you almost nothing.

steps.title: ⛔ Read the serial number FIRST — CVA recalled a range of in-lines
steps.action: Before you clean, load or fire anything, read the serial number off the gun and look at how it ENDS. In August 1997 CVA recalled every in-line with a serial ending -95 or -96, and no catalog listing can tell you whether yours is one of them — only the number stamped on your gun can. If it ends that way, stop here and call CVA. Do not clean it, do not load it, and do not let anyone else use it.
steps.aside: If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the gun under any circumstances.
steps.quote: In August of 1997, CVA implemented a Voluntary Recall of all in-line gun models with serial numbers ending in -95 or -96.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — VOLUNTARY RECALL

steps.title: ⛔ Smokeless powder, in ANY quantity, is not an option
steps.action: This one is worth reading before every session, not once. Modern smokeless powder in a muzzleloader produces pressures the gun was never built for. CVA's own line is that it will likely lead to severe injury or death and voids the warranty immediately. ⚠ And the trap is the NAME: "blackpowder" describes the formulation, not the colour — most smokeless powders are black too.
steps.aside: The use of modern smokeless powder will immediately void the warranty.
steps.quote: NEVER USE ANY QUANTITY OF MODERN SMOKELESS POWDER IN ANY MUZZLELOADER!
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — PROPELLANTS

steps.title: ⛔ The pistol does NOT take the rifle's magnum charge
steps.action: This is the one number that separates the pistol from the rifle it shares an action with. CVA asks for a MINIMUM of 50 grains by volume, and says the 150-grain "magnum" charge is not appropriate for the pistol because the barrel is too short to burn it — the extra powder does not add velocity, it just leaves fouling.
steps.aside: the 150 grain “magnum” charge is not appropriate due to the short barrel length
steps.quote: CVA recommends a minimum of 50 grains, by volume, of blackpowder or blackpowder substitute in your CVA muzzleloader pistol.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — MINIMUM AND MAXIMUM LOADS FOR OPTIMA V2 PISTOL

steps.title: Forend screw out, forend off
steps.action: Take the screw out of the CENTRE of the forend with a properly fitting screwdriver and pull the forend gently off the barrel. Properly fitting matters: a CVA forend screw is soft and a loose driver rounds it out in one go.
steps.quote: Using a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the screw from the center of the forend. Gently pull the forend off of the barrel.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: Breeching lever back, barrel off the action
steps.action: Pull the breeching lever to the rear and open the action. With the forend off, the barrel pivots forward and comes right off the action — that is what makes this gun easy to clean properly rather than approximately.
steps.quote: Pull the breeching lever to the rear and open the action. Without the forend in place the barrel will pivot forward and off of the action.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: Breech plug out, counter-clockwise, and set it SOAKING
steps.action: Turn the breech plug counter-clockwise and take it out, then wet it thoroughly with cleaning solvent and put it aside to soak while you do the bore. Doing it in that order is the difference between wiping a plug and scraping one.
steps.quote: Turn the breech plug in a counter-clockwise direction and remove. Wet the breech plug thoroughly with cleaning solvent and set aside.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: Wet patches first, then the brush, then patches to clean
steps.action: Jag on the rod, a patch or two wet with WATER through the barrel to carry the bulk of the fouling out. Then a properly fitting bore brush wet with solvent, several full-length strokes. Then solvent patches, let them work a minute or two, and follow with dry ones — repeat until the barrel is clean.
steps.aside: Place a properly fitting bore brush on the rod and make several full-length strokes through the barrel. The brush should be wet with solvent for this step.
steps.quote: Using a jag on a cleaning rod, range rod, or extended ram rod, push a patch or two wet with water through the barrel to remove the bulk of the fouling from the bore.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: ⛔ Non-petroleum oil in the bore
steps.action: Protect the bore with a good quality NON-PETROLEUM gun oil. That word is not decoration — petroleum oil and blackpowder fouling make a tar that is worse than either, and CVA names the alternative on the page.
steps.quote: Use a good quality non-petroleum gun oil to protect the bore.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: Breech plug: threads, front face, primer pocket, FLASH HOLE
steps.action: Wipe every surface of the soaked plug including the threads, and make sure the front, the primer pocket and the flash hole — the small hole through the centre — are clean. Cotton swabs, pipe cleaners and a nipple pick are the tools. ⛔ Then grease the threads generously with breech plug grease or high-temperature anti-seize and install it FINGER TIGHT. Over-tightening is what welds a plug into a barrel.
steps.aside: Generously apply breech plug grease or high temperature anti-seize to the breech plug threads and install into the barrel finger tight
steps.quote: Make sure the front is clean as well as the primer pocket and flash hole (the small hole through the center of the plug).
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

steps.title: Breech face and the action areas you can reach
steps.action: Solvent patch over the breech face and whatever else in the action you can get at, cotton swabs for the rest. Wipe it dry with a clean patch or rag and put rust preventative on it.
steps.aside: Wipe dry with a clean patch or rag and apply rust preventative.
steps.quote: Use a patch wet with solvent to scrub the breech face and other action areas that you can reach.
steps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

deepSteps.title: Firing pin bushing out — this is not optional maintenance
deepSteps.action: Remove the firing pin bushing from the front of the breech face with a properly fitting screwdriver; the firing pin and its spring drop out. Clean the parts AND the recess thoroughly, lubricate, and put a light coat of breech plug grease on the bushing threads. CVA calls this a very important part of maintaining the gun, and the reason is in the next step.
deepSteps.aside: Cleaning the firing pin assembly is a very important part of maintaining your gun.
deepSteps.quote: Using a properly fitting screwdriver remove the firing pin bushing from the front of the breech face. The firing pin and spring will drop out.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Then PROVE the firing pin retracts — or do not fire it
deepSteps.action: Pull the trigger rearward and press the hammer forward. The firing pin should be visible ONLY with the hammer pressed all the way forward, and it must recess back into the frame when the hammer is released. That proves the return spring is in and working. ⛔ If it does not behave that way, do not fire the gun. A pin seized OUT can drag on the cap as the breech closes and fire it; a pin seized IN will not fire at all.
deepSteps.aside: The firing pin should be visible only when the hammer is pressed all the way forward and it should recess into the frame once the hammer is released
deepSteps.cite: CVA Optima V2 / Wolf V2 Owner's Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code and no year is printed in this edition. — CLEANING PROCEDURE, printed p.12-13

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Wet patches (water) first to carry the bulk of the fouling out
Bore brush wet with solvent, several full-length strokes
Solvent patches, left to work a minute, then dry patches
Repeat until clean, then a NON-PETROLEUM oil to protect it

cleaning.name: BREECH PLUG
tasks: Soaked in solvent while the bore is done
⛔ Primer pocket and FLASH HOLE clear — swabs, pipe cleaners, pick
⛔ Threads greased with anti-seize, installed FINGER TIGHT only

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE & ACTION
tasks: Solvent patch and cotton swabs over what you can reach

cleaning.name: FIRING PIN ASSEMBLY
tasks: Bushing out, pin and spring cleaned with the recess
Light breech plug grease on the bushing threads
⛔ Retraction PROVED before the gun is fired again

reassembly: Firing pin, spring and bushing back in, bushing threads lightly greased.
⛔ Breech plug threads greased with breech plug grease or high-temperature anti-seize, installed FINGER TIGHT — never with a tool.
Barrel back onto the action, breeching lever closed.
Forend on and its centre screw tightened with a properly fitting driver.
⛔ Firing pin retraction checked before the gun is loaded.
fncheck: Reassembled: breech plug in finger tight with greased threads, barrel back on the action, forend on with its centre screw. ⛔ Then the firing pin check — trigger back, hammer pressed forward, pin visible only at full forward and recessing when the hammer is released. If it does not, the gun does not get fired. Finally, look through the barrel from the breech end and confirm you can see light before anything is loaded.
